title: LLM Scientific Reasoning: How to Make AI Capable of Nobel Prize Discoveries: Hubert Misztela
talk_summary: A Novartis researcher describes using RAG over pre-discovery literature to test whether LLMs can rediscover a Nobel-winning mechanism, arguing that complex questions need explicit reasoning steps before retrieval rather than naive embedding lookup. He shows that question decomposition, strict prompting, relevance classification, and clustering retrieved chunks by variance improved groundedness on a single hard question.

takeaways.what_they_do: They add explicit reasoning/routing over the question (decomposition, identifying multiple concepts) before embedding retrieval, instead of throwing the raw question at the vector store.
takeaways.evidence_quote: between more convoluted the semantics of the question um the more the harder is going to be for your standard track without those reasoning steps

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a fixed top-k, they cluster retrieval distances and keep only the top cluster with lowest within/between variance to decide how many chunks carry real signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can calculate the variances within the different clusters of those embeddings and between them so this is called genkins natural brakes

takeaways.what_they_do: They restrict the RAG corpus to documents dated before the known discovery so the model cannot cheat from pretraining, then measure whether it rediscovers the result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use Rag and in that rag we have only the the the the scientific papers from before the discovery right so that it doesn't cheat

takeaways.technique: Strict prompting to suppress pretrained leakage
takeaways.what_they_do: When the model answered from memorized knowledge instead of the provided corpus, they tightened the prompt to force grounding in retrieved documents only.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to make the The Prompt stronger right so we call it strict prompting and then it and it got better

takeaways.technique: Delegate reasoning types to specialist tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than expecting the LLM to do all reasoning, they route arithmetic/algorithmic reasoning to code execution and causal reasoning to dedicated libraries.
